blocks.text: Innovations in blockchain technology, known as Blockchain 2.0, introduce advanced features and capabilities beyond basic cryptocurrency applications. Blockchain 2.0 includes smart contracts, decentralized applications (dApps), and enhanced scalability.

Smart contracts are self-executing contracts with the terms of the agreement directly written into code. They automatically execute and enforce the contract terms when predefined conditions are met, reducing the need for intermediaries.

Example: In real estate, smart contracts can automate property transactions. When all conditions, such as payment and ownership verification, are met, the contract executes automatically, transfening ownership to the buyer and funds to the seller.
